document.title: AmEmbassy Kabul cable 7726 to SecState, "Meeting with President Amin"
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Soviet Invasion of Afghanistan, 1979: Not Trump’s Terrorists, Nor Zbig’s Warm Water Ports | National Security Archive
document.note: Report on Archer Blood's forty minutes alone with Amin on October 27, 1979, a missing link to Soviet paranoia. The Soviet record shows the meeting set off alarm bells for KGB chief Andropov. Blood concluded Amin genuinely wanted better U.S.-Afghan relations but seemed oblivious to how it would look in Moscow. Also published in FRUS 1977-80, Afghanistan, Vol. XII, pp. 218-222.

events.description: Archer Blood met alone with President Amin for forty minutes in Kabul.
Shoot-out in Kabul that left Amin the undisputed ruler of the Saur Revolution.
President Park of South Korea reportedly killed.
Ambassador Blood met President Amin alone for forty minutes at Kabul; the call was publicized on Afghan TV newscasts.
AmEmbassy Kabul cable 7726 sent to SecState reporting the Amin meeting.
Shoot-out in Kabul that left Amin the undisputed ruler of the Saur Revolution, referred to by Blood.
President Park Chung-hee of South Korea was killed the previous night, as Blood told Amin.
Death of Ambassador Adolph Dubs, referenced as the cause of U.S.-Afghan tension and the Pell-Stone amendment barrier.
Cable 7726 (section 3 of 3) from AmEmbassy Kabul to SecState reports Ambassador Blood's meeting with President Amin, with human rights discussion and the ambassador's impressions.
Blood met Amin and discussed human rights, foreign interference, and improving U.S.-Afghan relations. Amin said he could never sacrifice Afghan independence to the Soviets.

relationships.quote: RUPTURE OF RELATIONS KITH SQUTH KOREA, HAD BEEN TAKEN COM-PLETELY ON ITS OWN

relationships.detail: Amin attacked the human rights record of the Zahir and Daoud regimes, saying the Saur Revolution overthrew a regime serving one family.
relationships.quote: AMIN ATTACKED THE HUMAN RIGHTS RECORD OF THE PREVIOUS ZAHIR AND DAGUD REGIMES.

relationships.detail: Amin condemned the Daoud regime as part of Mohammedzai rule that imprisoned, tortured and executed people.

relationships.detail: Amin said that even if Brezhnev asked him to act against Afghan independence he would refuse.
relationships.quote: IF BREZHNEY HIMSELF SHOULD ASK HIM TO TAKE ANY ACTION AGAINST AFGHAN INOQEPENDENCE

relationships.detail: Amin claimed Congress was prepared to give ten million dollars to so-called Afghan refugees in Pakistan; Blood did not challenge that the USG was not aiding the insurgents.
relationships.quote: THE U.S.CONGRESS IS PREPAREO TO GIVE TEN MILLION DOLLARS TO SO-CALLED AFGHAN REFUGEES IN PAXISTAN

relationships.detail: Amin pressed Blood for U.S. development assistance and claimed the DRA had refrained from public criticism of the U.S.
relationships.quote: AMIN MADE A STRONG PITCH FOR UsS. MATERIAL ASSISTANCE.

relationships.detail: Amin discussed the American animosity after Ambassador Dubs' death and would not accept DRA responsibility for it.

relationships.detail: Blood told Amin of Park's killing to suggest a parallel to Amin's own consolidation of power; Amin showed no sympathy.
relationships.quote: I ASKED AMIN IF HE HEARD THE NEWS THAT PRESIOENT PARK HAD BEEN KILLEO THE PREVIQUS MIGHT.

key_claims: Amin sought improved U.S.-Afghan relations and U.S. development assistance but offered no concrete steps.
Amin claimed DRA foreign policy decisions (South Korea, Egypt, Polisario) were made without Soviet consultation.
Amin said Soviet aid was increasing and necessary for the DRA to withstand foreign interference, and did not dispute that the US was not aiding insurgents.
Blood assessed that Amin might seek better U.S. ties to sow doubt among insurgency supporters Pakistan, Iran and Saudi Arabia.
Amin did not acknowledge DRA responsibility for Ambassador Dubs' death and said nobody was out to kill Americans.
Blood judged Amin would be content with a limited, non-confrontational relationship.
